preview: Sarah: Let me take one quick look for an older DC06 build before we park it on JD.

messages.text: My DC06 miners are not mining correctly. I did an update from the Hammer WebSite for the DC06 miner and when I go to my mining pool dashboard it calls the miners Thor/P2
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · Hammer DC06 firmware pool shows Thor P2 model name

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

That "Thor/P2" name on the pool is a real clue. Your pool reads the model string the miner sends in its stratum login, so if it says Thor P2 the unit is almost certainly running a Thor P2 image instead of the DC06 one. The T. P2 is a SHA-256 (Bitcoin) machine and the DC06 is Scrypt, so with the wrong image on it the DC06 will not hash properly on your Doge/LTC pool.

One thing first, so I send you to the right file:

1. Open the miner's web UI and go to the System or Settings page.
2. Tell me exactly what it shows for firmware version and for model/board.

A screenshot of that page is perfect if it is easier.

Also useful in the same message: the filename you downloaded from the Hammer site, and whether the pool is showing any accepted shares at all or zero.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that screenshot tells me a lot. Here is what I read on it:

- Norn OS, badge DC06, board V02, firmware 3.0.1 20261012, chip MSBT0501
- Hashrate flat at about 350 MH/s over 15 minutes, which is above the 330 MH/s rating
- Hashboard 47 C, VRM 63 C, fan 71 percent (2009 RPM), 84.1 W at 12.1 V, ASIC 2300 MHz
- Pool us1.letsmine.it:3344, worker ...····, uptime just under 2 hours

So the unit itself is healthy and it is a Scrypt DC06, not a Thor P2. It is hashing at full rated speed and running cool.

The "Thor/P2" on the pool dashboard is a label, not what the miner is doing. The pool prints the model string the firmware announces when it logs in, and the shared Norn OS builds carry one string across several Hammer models, so a DC06 can show up under the wrong name after an update. Nothing about your hashing changes from it.

Let me check one thing before we go further: on your letsmine.it dashboard, what does it show for the worker ···· as accepted shares and as the 1 hour or 24 hour average hashrate? If that number sits near 330 to 350 MH/s, everything is working and the name is cosmetic. If it is zero or far below, we have a real pool-side problem and I will dig into the stratum side.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That second shot confirms it from the other side:

- Model name: DC06
- Firmware version: 3.0.1 20261012
- "Your firmware is up to date"

So the correct DC06 image is on the unit. You did not flash a Thor P2 by mistake. The firmware just sends a generic Norn OS device string at stratum login and the pool prints whatever it gets, which is why letsmine.it is labelling it Thor/P2. Cosmetic, not a mining fault.

The one thing still open is whether the pool is actually crediting the work. On your letsmine.it dashboard for worker ····, tell me:

1. the accepted shares count (is it climbing?)
2. the 1 hour or 24 hour average hashrate the pool shows

If that pool average is somewhere around 300 to 350 MH/s, your miners are mining correctly and only the name is wrong. If it is zero or way low, say so and I will go into the Logs tab with you to read the stratum lines.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Handed to the team · Cosmetic firmware bug I cannot fix from support: DC06 image sends the Thor P2 st

That screenshot settles it. Good news: your miners are mining correctly.

What I see in Last submits:

- All three rigs (····) are submitting shares, several per 10 to 20 seconds
- Share diffs vary normally (1.14, 2.31, 5.45, 26.61, 22.66), which is exactly what a healthy Scrypt worker looks like
- Each row carries the tag THOR/P2/1.0.0

That tag is the stratum "user agent" string, the name the firmware sends itself as when it logs into the pool. In the 3.0.1 DC06 build that string is left as THOR/P2/1.0.0, so letsmine.it prints Thor P2 next to every one of your DC06 workers. It is a label only. The work being submitted is Scrypt work from your DC06s, the pool is accepting it, and you are being credited normally under your own rig names.

Nothing for you to change: do not reflash, and keep the firmware where it is since 3.0.1 is current.

I have passed the wrong user agent string on to JD, our hardware lead, as a firmware report. If you want to talk to him directly he is very active on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

One last sanity check if you want it: compare the pool's 24 hour average for each rig against roughly 330 MH/s each. If one of the three sits well below the other two, tell me which and we will look at that unit.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. These lines are noise, not a fault.

What the log says: something on your network keeps asking the miner's web server for a page called /probe, the firmware does not serve that address, so it answers 404 Not Found and logs a warning. "W" is a warning, not an error. Three lines get written per request (the 404, the send result, the handler), which is why it looks dramatic.

Note the timestamps: 08:19 and 08:20, repeating every 25 seconds or so. That is a poller on your LAN, typically:

- a phone or desktop miner monitoring app scanning the subnet
- a home automation or network scanner (Home Assistant, Fing, a router device scan)
- a second browser tab or a dashboard left open on an old page

None of it touches hashing. Your miners were submitting shares at the same time those lines were written.

If you want the log quiet:

1. Close any miner app or dashboard page watching that IP and reload the Logs tab after a few minutes.
2. If the lines keep coming, it is a scanner on the network rather than the miner, and you can safely ignore them.

So where we stand: hardware fine, firmware correct and current, pool accepting shares from all three rigs, the Thor P2 name is a label from the firmware's stratum string which is now with JD. Anything else looking off to you?
Since this update I can long longer merge mine

Merge mining is decided at the pool, not in the miner. The D.06 only sends Scrypt shares; the pool is what attaches the Dogecoin (and Luckycoin, Bells, etc.) aux chains to them. So firmware 3.0.1 cannot switch merge mining off by itself. What an update can do is wipe or shorten the pool user field, and your worker is logging in as an LTC address only.

Let me check how letsmine.it expects merge mining to be set, one minute.
Searched the web · letsmine.it merge mining dogecoin setup username address

Here is the key thing: the DC06 cannot turn merge mining on or off. Merge mining happens at the pool, which attaches the Doge (and other aux chain) work to the same Scrypt share. The miner just hashes what it is given. So the update did not disable it, but it very likely rewrote your pool settings, and that is where merge mining is selected.

Two things set it on a merged pool: the port you connect to, and the format of the user field. Right now your worker logs in as:

···· on us1.letsmine.it:3344

That is an LTC address plus a rig name, with no second address. On merged pools the username usually carries both chains, something like LTCaddress.DOGEaddress.rigname, and some pools use a separate port for the merged work.

I searched and could not find published letsmine.it merged mining docs I would trust, so I will not guess their exact format.

Two questions and we will have it:

1. Do you remember what the user field looked like before the update? Was there a second address or extra text after the LTC address?
2. On your letsmine.it account page, what does their own setup or help section give as the stratum port and username format for merged DOGE mining?

If you have a screenshot of that pool setup page, send it and I will map it onto the Pool tab of all three miners.
This is what the pool has me do

That screenshot answers it. The pool's own generator takes three things: your LTC wallet address, the Rig Id, and a separate DOGE address, with the note that merged mining needs the DOGE address to pay DOGE rewards.

Your miners are logging in with the LTC address and the rig name only. The D. part is missing, which is exactly why the Doge side stopped after the update: the update rewrote the pool fields and dropped whatever carried your DOGE address. Most pools put that second address either in the user string or in the password field, and letsmine's generator is what tells us which.

Next step, on this same screen:

1. The form is already filled with your LTC address, Rig Id ···· and your DOGE address. Leave difficulty on AUTO, and pick USA since it shows 51 ms and Poland is offline.
2. Click G. config.
3. Tell me exactly what it gives for the stratum URL, the port, the user field and the password field. Blank out nothing, just do not send me anything that looks like an account password.

Then we put those four values into each miner's Pool tab (one rig at a time, changing only the Rig Id to ···· and ····), save and restart. One note already: the DC06 only has one user field, so if the generator puts the DOGE address in the password field, that field must be copied exactly, not left at "x".
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That is the answer. Look at the Password field:

diff=auto;doge=····;notif=...

On letsmine.it the DOGE address is carried in the stratum password, not in the user name. Your user string is unchanged and correct, so the firmware update wiped the password field (it likely sits at "x" or empty now), and a share with no doge= tag gets credited on Litecoin only. That is the whole fault.

The fix, on each miner:

1. Open the miner's Pool tab.
2. Leave Pool URL us1.letsmine.it and port 3344 as they are. They work and the generator's Pool url line only complains because the region selector is still on Poland, which is offline.
3. Leave the User field as it is, with the rig name matching that unit (····).
4. Paste the whole password string from the generator into the password field, exactly as shown, semicolons included, no spaces. Use the copy icon on the right of the field so nothing gets cut.
5. Save, then Restart the miner.
6. Repeat on the other two.

Two things to watch:

- If the password field truncates what you paste, shorten it to diff=auto;doge=YOURDOGEADDRESS and drop the notif part. The doge= tag is the one that matters for merge mining.
- After the restart, check the pool page again in 10 to 15 minutes. The D. side should start crediting against the same shares, and your LTC hashrate should not change at all.

Tell me what the pool shows after the restart and we will confirm all three are merged.
It’s not showing on the Doge pool

Let me check one thing before we change anything else.

Send me a screenshot of the miner's Pool tab now, after the save and restart, so I can see the user field and whether the password line stuck (some firmware shows it as dots, that is fine, I mainly want to see the length and that it is not "x").

Two things worth knowing meanwhile:

1. You are on letsmine's solo side (the tab reads ltc Solo mining). On a solo merged setup the doge= address is where the aux reward is paid if one of your shares solves a block. It does not usually create a live hashrate page on the Doge side, because there are no continuous Doge payouts to show. If what you saw before the update was a DOGE entry with hashrate, tell me what page that was and I will look at it from that angle.
2. The miner cannot be "on the Doge pool" separately: there is only one connection, one set of shares, and the pool decides which chains those shares count for.

So: the Pool tab screenshot, and tell me where exactly you used to see the Doge side (same letsmine page, or a different site).
Before I did the update I could see the miners on the doge pool page

That fits exactly. On letsmine.it the Doge pool page lists workers by the DOGE address, and it only sees them when the shares arrive carrying the doge= tag in the password. No tag, no listing, which is what you have now.

So the one thing I need is whether the tag is actually going out after the update. Send me the Pool tab screenshot of one miner and I can tell you in a second:

- if the password field is empty or "x", the paste did not save and we will redo it
- if the full diff=auto;doge=... string is sitting there and the Doge page still shows nothing after 15 minutes, then 3.0.1 is not passing the password through to the pool, which is a firmware regression and goes straight to JD

Also tell me whether the Doge page is still empty for all three rigs or just some.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Good, that tells me a lot. Stratum Host and Stratum User are right. The S. Password shows only five dots, which looks like a short leftover value such as "x" rather than the 80 character string from the generator. Some firmware masks with a fixed number of dots, so let us confirm rather than assume.

1. Tap the small eye / reveal icon at the right end of the Stratum Password field and tell me what it actually contains.

If it is not the full diff=auto;doge=...;notif=... string:

2. Select everything in that field and delete it.
3. Copy the password line from the letsmine generator with its copy icon and paste it in.
4. Press SAVE, then RESTART.
5. Come back to this Pool tab after the reboot and reveal the field again, to confirm the whole string survived the save. That is the step that matters: if it saves as five characters again, the firmware is truncating it and that is JD's to fix.

Do it on this one (phone hidden)) first and tell me what you see.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That is the string in place: diff=auto;doge=... saved, and it kept the doge address (the notif part is optional, no problem). The banner says Successfully saved and the button now reads Pending Restart.

1. Press Pending Restart and let it come back up (about a minute).
2. Return to this Pool tab and check the password field still shows the full diff=auto;doge=... line. If it does, the setting stuck.
3. Repeat the same paste on the other two miners, changing nothing else. Their Stratum User keeps its own rig name, ···· and ····.
4. Give it 10 to 15 minutes of hashing, then open the Dogecoin page on letsmine.it and look up your DOGE address. The rigs should appear there again as they did before the update.

Tell me what the Doge page shows after that and we will know if all three are merged again.
This right before the restart

Understood, so that shot was the state just before you hit restart.

Go ahead and press Pending Restart on that unit now. When it comes back:

1. Reopen the Pool tab and confirm the Stratum Password still reads diff=auto;doge=... in full.
2. Then do the same paste, save and restart on the other two miners, keeping each one's own rig name in the Stratum User field.

Once all three are back up and hashing for about 10 to 15 minutes, look up your DOGE address on the letsmine.it Dogecoin page and tell me whether the rigs show there. If they do, you are merged again and we are done. If the password field comes back short or the Doge page stays empty with the full string in place, that points at 3.0.1 not passing the password to the pool, and I will put it in front of JD with your details.
Here is the pool page on the miner after the restart

After a reload the field goes back to masked, and those five dots may just be a fixed placeholder rather than five real characters. One click settles it:

Tap the eye icon at the right of the Stratum Password field and tell me what it shows.

- Full diff=auto;doge=... line: the setting survived the restart, and we move on to the other two miners and then check the Doge page.
- Anything short like x: the firmware did not keep it, and that is a 3.0.1 bug I will take to JD with your exact details.
It’s just *****

Then the UI never reveals it, so we cannot judge from that field. The pool is the honest test: if the doge= tag is going out, the Doge page will list the rig.

1. Leave that miner running as it is now, roughly 15 minutes.
2. In the meantime do the same paste, save and restart on the other two, each with its own rig name.
3. Then look up your DOGE address on the letsmine.it Dogecoin page.

If the rigs appear there, the password did save and the UI is just masking it. If the Doge page is still empty after 15 minutes of shares, then 3.0.1 is dropping the stratum password and that is a firmware fault, not something you can fix from the settings. Tell me which way it goes and I will take it straight to JD with your firmware build, the pool and the config.
Ok

Sounds good. Take your time with the other two and come back here when the Doge page has had 15 minutes to catch up.

Quick recap of where we are, so nothing gets lost:

- Hardware and firmware fine on all three DC06, 3.0.1 20261012 is current
- The T. P2 name on the pool is just the firmware's stratum string, already reported to JD
- Merge mining lives in the stratum password (diff=auto;doge=...), which the update wiped. That is what we are restoring now

If you would rather compare notes live while you wait, JD and a lot of DC06 owners are on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
Here id the Doge pool page after 15 minutes and the last 4 of my address is ····

Thanks. Important detail in that list: those rigs are shown by DOGE address (····), and none of them ends in ····. So that is the pool-wide Doge view, not yours, and your address is not in the visible rows. The list is also cut off at the bottom.

One check before I call it a firmware fault:

1. Use the search box at the top of letsmine.it (the "Your wallet address" field) and paste your DOGE address, the one ending ····.
2. Send me what that page shows: any active workers, any hashrate, any recent submits.

That page is per address, so if your three rigs are being credited on the Doge side they will show there even when they are far down the pool-wide list. If that page is empty too, I have everything I need to hand it to JD as a 3.0.1 password regression.
My miners are not on there
Handed to the team · Merge mining broken after the official DC06 update; stratum password does not re

That settles it, and it is not something you can fix from the settings page.

What we proved together:

- LTC side is perfect: all three rigs hashing around 330 to 350 MH/s and submitting shares every few seconds
- The pool needs diff=auto;doge=... in the stratum password for merge mining
- You pasted it, it saved, you restarted, and 15 minutes later your DOGE address page still lists no workers
- The password field reads back as five masked dots and the eye never reveals the stored value

So firmware 3.0.1 20261012 looks like it is truncating or dropping the stratum password, which kills the doge tag and with it the Doge side. The L. mining keeps working because that part rides on the user field, which is intact.

I have put all of it in front of JD, our hardware lead: model, build, pool, the exact config and what the pool shows. The team has it and will confirm by email, usually within one business day. Stay in the chat if you can, someone may jump in here directly.

One thing to avoid in the meantime: do not press SAVE on the Pool tab without re-pasting the password first, since the field may write those masked dots back over your string.

Faster route if you want it tonight: JD is active on our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate and point him at firmware 3.0.1 20261012 dropping the stratum password on the DC06. He can tell you whether to sit tight for a fixed build or go back to the previous official one.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That confirms it from the pool's own side. Your DOGE address page reads:

- "Nobody is mining at this moment", last submit seen 27 years ago, which is their way of saying never in this epoch
- Hashrate 5m and 60m both 0 H/s, flat line across 24h
- An all-time best share of 53.77 K, so the address has seen work in the past, just nothing now

So zero doge-tagged shares are reaching the pool even with the string pasted and the unit restarted. That is exactly the evidence JD needs and it is already with him, along with your build, your pool and your config.

Worth saying clearly: nothing is being lost on the Litecoin side. Your three DC06 keep hashing and submitting there as normal, you just are not getting the aux Doge chance attached until the password reaches the pool.

The team has it and will confirm by email, usually within one business day. If you want to move faster tonight, JD is on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate and tell him 3.0.1 20261012 on the DC06 is not sending the stratum password.
I wish I could go back to the previous version for the DC06 miner, because I knew it worked with the merged mining

That is a reasonable instinct, and it is mechanically possible: the Settings page has a Browse field that takes a .bin, so the unit will accept an older build if you have the correct file.

Three cautions before you do it:

1. It must be the official DC06 .bin from Hammer. Never another model's file and never an unofficial build. A Thor P2 or DC02 image on a DC06 is how people brick these.
2. Check your tablet or computer Downloads folder first. If you still have the .bin you flashed before this one, that is your rollback file.
3. Flash with Preserve User Data unchecked if the downgrade misbehaves, and expect to re-enter the pool host, user and that password string afterwards.

What I cannot do is hand you an older build, since I do not host or publish the firmware. The person who can point you at the right earlier DC06 file, or tell you a fixed build is the better wait, is JD. He already has your case, and he is quickest on Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate and say 3.0.1 20261012 dropped the stratum password and you want the previous DC06 build.

If you find an older .bin yourself and want a second pair of eyes before flashing, paste me the filename and version and I will check it is the DC06 one.
The screen in this picture for the DC06 miner was the one that was working great with the merged mining

I opened it. That photo shows the DC06 running the older stock Hammer screen layout: the left panel with MSBTC501, 11.79 V, 3824 mV, 3115 mA and the power reading, the right panel with the Hammer DC06 logo and 259.0 MH/s. That is the pre Norn OS interface, which is a very useful marker.

So the change was not just a version bump. The update moved the unit from the old Hammer build to the Norn OS 3.0.1 line, and the stratum password handling (plus that THOR/P2 device string) came with it. That matches everything we have seen.

Two things that would make the rollback easy if you can find them:

1. Did the old screen or its web page show a version number anywhere, something like 2.x? If you remember it, that names the file you want.
2. Check your Downloads folder for the .bin you flashed before this one.

Keep this photo. Show it to JD along with the version, it tells him immediately which build you were on. He is on Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate. Your case is already with him and the team will confirm by email, usually within one business day.
